In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best prognostic score has not yet been defined, but the Saps II is the one that best predicts mortality.
the Saps II score, associated with the Iget, is the best predictive score of severity of acute pancreatitis, being able to predict the severity of the disease in the first 12 h of evolution.
there is no single score that can predict the severity of acute pancreatitis with certainty, but that the combination of different scores may increase the accuracy of the prediction.

the choice of the best score for a specific service, is a complex and dynamic process, which is still in evolution.
the use of the scores is not a routine, but a decision of the professional, according to the characteristics of the patient, the service where he works and his experience.

, the use of predictive scores for severity of acute pancreatitis, in the context of the Brazilian public health system, is still incipient, but with the development of the medical residency and postgraduate courses, the use of these scores will increase.

the use of predictive factors is important to identify the patients with a higher risk of developing severe acute pancreatitis and to guide the therapeutic approach.
the use of predictive scores for acute pancreatitis is still a challenge for health services.
the choice of a predictive score is not an easy task and it should be done by the physician who will be in charge of the patient's follow-up.
